narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed and, based on an automated assessment of your financial profile, you were identified as a potential credit risk, resulting in the denial of your application. The model estimated a 51% probability that you represent a bad credit risk — a figure that sits right on the boundary, meaning this was not a clear-cut decision, but just enough uncertainty to tip the outcome toward denial. Understanding what drove this outcome can help you take meaningful steps to strengthen your position for a future application.

The single most influential factor working against you was the current status of your checking account, which shows a negative balance. Among applicants who were approved, only about 1 in 5 had a negative checking account balance, while roughly half of approved applicants had no checking account at all or maintained a positive balance. A negative balance signals to the assessment that you may already be under financial strain, making it harder to take on additional debt responsibly.

The second most important factor was your credit history, which was recorded as having no prior credits or all credits fully paid — a category that sounds positive on the surface, but is actually quite rare among approved applicants, representing only about 2% of those who were approved. The vast majority of approved applicants had a history of existing paid credits or even some past difficulties that were resolved, which gives the model more evidence of how you handle ongoing debt obligations. Without that track record, there is simply less information to confirm your ability to manage a loan over time.

On a more positive note, your property ownership — specifically owning real estate — actually worked in your favor and pushed the assessment toward a better credit outcome. This is a meaningful asset that demonstrates financial stability, and it is something you can continue to highlight in future applications.

It is also worth noting that your installment rate of 4% of disposable income is higher than the average of approximately 2.94% among approved applicants, and you already have 2 existing credits at the bank compared to an average of about 1.4 among approved applicants — both of which may add to the perception of financial pressure, even if they were not the top drivers of this decision.

Given how close the predicted probability was to the threshold, relatively modest improvements to your financial profile could make a real difference. The most impactful step you could take would be to bring your checking account into a positive balance and maintain it there for a period of time before reapplying. Building a visible credit track record — for example, by successfully managing a smaller credit product — would also help address the gap in your credit history. Speaking directly with a bank advisor could give you a clearer roadmap, as they may be able to consider context that an automated system cannot fully capture.
